commits.message:
Hold wallet-only fault-proof sends until one validity window after restart

A transaction that spends only wallet coins has no input of ours that
excludes a duplicate, so a copy built before a restart could land beside
a rebuilt one. The shared runner now holds such a transaction after its
preflight and before anything is journaled or sent, returning pending
under the named state fault_proof_restart_wait until the caller's
restart wait opens. It also refuses one that carries no upper validity
bound, or one later than the caller's latest wallet-only slot (one
window past the caller's clock, plus one slot of rounding).

The caller owns both answers through one walletOnlySend object, on its
own clock: the watcher builds it once per process from its clock, the
follower's applied cursor and the deployment rule bundle's slot config;
the CLI uses a clock-only wait. The watcher supervisor does not admit a
job held by the wait again until the wait has opened, so a held
objective is preflighted once while the wait is closed, and its
readiness hold stays visible for the whole wait.

Bound wallet-only fault-proof transactions to a three-minute validity window

Init, proof chunk publication, transition-trace data carriage, script-decode
stage and Bind, field-preimage certification, field-grammar Open and CEK
staging spend only wallet coins, so a copy rebuilt after a restart could land
beside the original. Each now carries an upper validity bound from one shared
helper (walletOnlyValidTo, WALLET_ONLY_VALIDITY_MS = 180000), held to at most
half of the worst-case proof-time bound on the shortest-maturity profile.
No lower bound is set.

The field-preimage carriage publication stays unbounded: a full chunk's
publication already sits exactly on the publication size target. A duplicate
costs only an output's min-ada, which the proof-materials sweep recovers.
Goal spec row W33 states the exception.

Tests pin the bound on every bounded kind, the publication exemption, and
ledger refusal of a stale init and chunk publication with acceptance of a
rebuilt one. Step transcripts are regenerated: bounded rows gain a ttl, and
later rows move only in redeemer ledger-order indices that follow from the
earlier transactions' new hashes.

Give the DA committee node's declaration build a 6 GB heap

The tsup declaration build needs between 3.5 and 4 GB of heap. Under
Node's default it runs out of memory on the CI runners, which fails the
package's tests and the installed-boundary check at their prerequisite
build. Set the heap the way midgard-node's build steps do.

Submit the Present-maximum journey's steps after building them

The forced step builders return a signed transaction and no longer
submit. The journey still called them directly, so each step-1 capture
saw no submission and all twelve maximum-fit cases failed.

Confirm the carriage the tier-3 action chains publish in their journal

The healing chains serve republished field chunks and the certificate as
outputs of transactions the workflow confirmed, as a real run journals them.
The suite's top-level fixtures move to a support module so the file stays
under its size ceiling.

Journal the carriage the network-id forced harness serves as the workflow's own

The adapter claims field carriage only among outputs of transactions its
journal confirmed, so the harness now hands the adapter a confirmed entry for
every transaction it serves at the materials and certificate addresses. The
entry builder is shared with the double-spend carriage harness.
Give the family assembly fixture its proof-materials address and count a tagged refund in the top-up test

Reset the commit-base fixture's tables before taking the follower write gate

The fixture reset inside its gated write, so a follower view an earlier file
applied in the same worker database refused it. The node fast tier packs
confirmed-ledger-generation after such a file and failed three of its tests.

Keep the scripted defender's agreed hashes and memoised nodes in one buffer per level

Each agreed state hash was a 32-byte pooled Buffer copy, and each kept one
pinned an 8 KiB Buffer pool slab: about 900 MB in a max-shape dispute
worker. Worker peak RSS drops from 3.70 to 2.58 GB on the builtin-semantic
max-shape dispute and from 4.07 to 3.02 GB on the writeBits loop.

Split the nested-list walk-cost gate rows and the maximum transition-trace lifecycle by case

The two nested-list gate groups (1,190 and 1,039 CI seconds) become one file per row, and the honest-root refusal at the maximum transition-trace shape moves beside the conviction into its own file, so their plays run in parallel. Test names, shapes and timeouts are unchanged.

Fault-proof builders return a signed transaction and never submit

Each builder used to build, sign, call an optional pre-submit boundary and
then submit. The workflow adapters passed a boundary that threw to carry
the signed transaction out, so the code after it never ran in production,
and a caller that omitted the boundary submitted with no record.

Builders now stop at the signed transaction and return it. Adapters call
them directly and keep the checks they ran on the built transaction. The
capture exception and the boundary parameter are gone.

- A builder that sent several transactions in one call returns the next
  one as a turn; the CLI and tests loop over turns.
- Removal is split into a builder for one removal and a driver that owns
  the lease from acquisition to release. The driver fails the lease on an
  error in any pass.
- Direct submission has one name, submitUnjournaled, and a lint guard
  keeps it and the turn submitters out of the watcher, the node and the
  workflow code. Field-grammar certification still submits its batches
  itself and is the one builder-side exception.
- The CLI submission gate is an allow-list: a command or init category
  that is neither admitted nor retired is refused before any provider
  access.
- Submitting drivers with no production caller are deleted, and the two
  in-process provers that only tests used move to test support.

Refresh the CI file duration tables from Node CI runs 44252349699, 44209831618 and 43921606823

The committed tables predated about a quarter of the fault-proof seconds and most of the node and watcher seconds, so shards were unbalanced and the tiers would have been drawn from stale weights. The traced-refusal reservation moves to the median of the same runs.

Split the fault-proof, node and watcher suites into fast and slow tiers by CI seconds

A file at or over 60 CI seconds in its package's duration table is in the slow tier, every other file in the fast tier. MIDGARD_TEST_TIER selects one; unset, as in CI, the whole suite runs. contrib test takes --tier fast|slow and the packages gain test:fast and test:slow.

Update the mint-authorization and transition-trace step transcripts for the script-locked proof-materials address

Each changed lifecycle's first changed transaction is the first that pays
the proof-materials address; lifecycles that pay it nothing are unchanged.
Step digests change for transactions paying it and for those whose datums
or redeemers carry the changed hashes; the rest change only their hashes
through wallet change. Row counts are unchanged.
Delete the obsolete size exception of the event-history capture test
